findings.summary: On the current winner, Census spends 95.6% of time in OCR. A 3,252-token page-5 region leaves one recognizer busy while the other three are largely idle.
observations: Median full Census call: 25.74 s; OCR 24.60 s; embedding 1.03 s. Shares use mean wall times.
In all three ordinary measurements, the longest page-5 region generated 3,252 tokens on GPU 3. Every region ended with raw EOS.
Measured OCR GPU-busy means were 6.3%, 9.5%, 4.9% and 98.4% for GPUs 0–3, using 73–74 one-second samples per GPU. GPU 3 averaged 70.7 W at the fixed 72 W limit.

One warm-up and three ordinary calls are separate from the bounded trace. The complete instrumented output passed the original frozen reference. The trace covers early engine iterations; telemetry covers the full measured OCR windows.
The servers were restarted with exactly the evaluation configuration. Actual launch commands, GPU UUIDs and batch-invariance environment are recorded with this profile.
Busy percentage and power do not measure percentage of peak compute or memory bandwidth. The measured imbalance and long sequence identify the remaining critical path.
findings.next_step: After the embedding screen, test within-request n-gram speculative decoding, requiring exact frozen OCR and EOS.
findings.optimization: Keep the four L4 GPUs, server concurrency eight, BF16 embeddings, window 64, dynamic pages and frozen references. Propose tokens within the current request only; accept a gain only through the unchanged full evaluator.
